summary.title: Day 8: minitest (Nim Days)
summary.one_liner: Learn how to build a small unit-test framework in Nim using a template (check) that prints the source text of an expression, and a statement macro (suite) that groups checks and indents their output.
keywords: build a test framework in nim
takeaways: Templates with untyped parameters and astToStr can print an expression's source text alongside a pass/fail result, removing doAssert message boilerplate.
A statement macro receives the block's statements as an AST (nnkCall nodes), and can inspect and rewrite them, e.g. adding an indent argument to check calls.
dumpTree is a practical way to visualize the AST of a code snippet while developing a macro.
Macros return a statement list built with newStmtList, newCall, newStrLitNode and newIntLitNode, which the compiler then inserts into the program.
summary.summary: The post is part of the Nim Days series and reimplements a unittest-style DSL inspired by a Practical Common Lisp chapter. It starts by showing the repetition in doAssert messages, then defines a check template that uses astToStr to print each expression with passed or failed. It then adds a suite statement macro that groups checks under a heading and indents them, explaining how dumpTree helps inspect the AST. The full code is in the xmonader/nim-minitest repository.
